definition: Coalesce means to merge into one unified whole.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word coalesce. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know coalesce should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: What began as three separate jam sessions in three garages slowly coalesced into a single band with one name.
Mingling is much weaker than coalescing — mingled guests and swirled streams stay themselves, each part still there to pick out, while things that coalesce grow into one whole.
Fuse goes further than coalesce — coalesced things have grown into one whole, but fused things have melted together past any hope of separating.

Merge means to combine into one, and it is usually a deliberate act with a date on it — two lanes of traffic, two school districts, two computer files, joined by decision. Coalesce is the unplanned version: separate things drift together and slowly grow into one whole, on their own schedule.

Unite means to join into one body on purpose — people unite behind a cause, states unite by treaty, and someone decides to do it. Coalesce needs no decision at all: nobody plans it, and the parts simply grow together until a single whole remains.

Coalesce is for gradual, unplanned joining: separate things drift, touch, and grow together into one whole.
If a merger is decreed on a Tuesday and done by Friday, that is combination by order — coalescing takes its own time.
Coalesce is the slow, unplanned way separate things become one — droplets, footpaths, movements.

When the joining is decided and dated, use merge; when people are called together on purpose, this unit's convene is the word; and when currents of events flow to one meeting point, that is a confluence.
